tasks.short: Enter and validate GIS source data

steps.what: Prepare source data and specify coordinate and attribute mappings
Digitize map features or resolve source values needing manual interpretation
Convert and enter specified digital records into the GIS database
Check entered geometry, attributes and source agreement

tasks.design: Configure the {OTHER} GIS import tools for known source formats and explicit coordinate or attribute mappings. Keep scanning, uncertain feature digitising and source interpretation with the technician; imports land in a draft dataset for geographic checks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Known-format records may need repeated interactive conversion and entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Saved native import jobs can reuse a specified mapping without interpreting an unfamiliar map.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous features, incomplete metadata and plausible-looking coordinates in the wrong reference system.
tasks.human_edge: The technician checks whether the geometry represents the intended real feature.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated conversion setup or entry while retaining source interpretation and data-quality responsibility.

reach.learn: Document coordinate, accuracy and interpretation constraints

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native GIS tools can import known digital formats and transform coordinates using explicit mappings; interpretation of ambiguous map features remains separate.

assumptions: Boundary is source entry into the maintained GIS database; project analysis and export tasks are separately counted. Entry methods are alternatives across cases, not a requirement to scan and digitise every digital table.

Source surveyor or data custodian supplies raw coordinates, attributes and source metadata as existing upstream work. Technician captures source ID, source and target coordinate reference systems, units, field mapping, feature identifier and handling of nulls in s1's 25 hours; scanning and source preparation are included there. S2's 35 hours retain all manual digitising or interpretation. Missing metadata or unsupported conversion stops the import for manual resolution, costed below.
Test native GIS import configuration first; the 25% share must be observed manual transfer or repeated setup, not existing conversion runtime or digitising directly into the final database.
No automatic geometry-correct or source-trustworthy flag is assumed; s4 checks representative locations and attribute meaning.
research_questions: Can saved import jobs reproduce the manually entered data without increasing coordinate or attribute errors?

already_counted.description: Source preparation, mapping capture and manual interpretation

incremental.description: Import mapping upkeep and unsupported-source correction

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=75, gross=25 and net=19 after six upkeep hours. Range assumes a mixed manual and digital entry workload; manual digitising and source checks retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Interpret aerial or ortho photographs to identify relevant features
Cross-check photograph interpretations against other evidence and record uncertainty

tasks.design: Retain interpretation and cross-checking in the {OTHER} GIS imagery viewer. The digest provides no validated aerial-feature classifier for this task, so a new image model is not assigned a labour saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Appearance depends on scale, date, shadows and the feature definition.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing imagery and reference layers support interpretation but are not a new automation gain.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing visually similar features and stating what the image cannot establish.
tasks.human_edge: The technician relates image patterns to the geographic context and corroborating evidence.
tasks.altitude: Imagery interpretation and uncertainty responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Describe resolution, acquisition date and visibility constraints

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: interpreting aerial imagery requires geographic context and attention to acquisition and visibility limits.

assumptions: Boundary is photograph interpretation, excluding image acquisition, database import and field verification undertaken by other roles.

Existing imagery custodian provides image, acquisition date, resolution and coordinate reference metadata. Technician checks these and establishes feature meaning within s1's 70 hours; missing metadata or ambiguous features remain unresolved for manual enquiry, never an automatic class label.
Use native imagery tools and reference overlays before adding software; current runtime earns no saving.
Zero upkeep because no new model, tool or process is introduced.
research_questions: Which feature types cannot be distinguished reliably from the available imagery alone?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross and net=0. No task-specific validated classifier is established and all interpretation effort remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Process and report geographic project data

steps.what: Specify project data, analysis purpose and required conversion or transfer
Convert and transfer specified project data using the GIS application
Analyze processed geographic data and check its meaning
Report the findings and prepare the checked project data handover

tasks.design: Save repeatable project conversion and transfer operations as native {OTHER} GIS processing jobs. The technician still defines the purpose, checks geographic meaning and writes the findings in {DOCS}; the processing job does not choose the analysis.
tasks.previous_blocker: A project may repeat the same interactive conversion and transfer operations for each source refresh.
tasks.enabler_now: Native processing models can replay explicit operations against versioned inputs.
tasks.still_hard: A technically successful operation can answer the wrong geographic question.
tasks.human_edge: The technician checks whether the result supports the intended conclusion.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated processing setup and more attention to findings and limitations.

reach.learn: Trace a conclusion to source versions and selected operations

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: GIS processing models can replay explicit conversion and transfer operations; analytical meaning still requires a person.

assumptions: Boundary is project processing and internal handover, excluding maintained-database entry owned by the separate entry task. Any operation serving both is allocated once in a local roll-up.

Technician produces source dataset IDs and versions, selected area, input and output coordinate systems, operation parameters, field mapping, output format and internal destination in s1's 30 hours. Source custodians supply datasets as existing upstream work. Missing metadata or unsupported schema stops the job for manual processing within exceptions; no analysis choice is inferred.
Try native GIS processing models before custom scripts; savings require observed repeated setup and transfer touches, not unattended computation or existing runtime.
External publication or transfer beyond the approved internal project boundary requires a separate local release decision and is not automated here.
research_questions: Can a saved job reproduce a manually prepared project package with unchanged geographic meaning?

already_counted.description: Processing choices and exact parameter capture

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=70, gross=30 and net=23 after seven upkeep hours. Range assumes a repeated manual-processing workload; analysis and reporting keep all their effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design and program GIS applications or procedures

steps.what: Clarify GIS application requirements and acceptance examples
Design geographic data models, interfaces and processing rules
Program the designed GIS application or procedure in development tools

loop.purpose: Draft a small implementation from the chosen GIS design
loop.input: Versioned design, interface definitions, selected repository context and non-sensitive test examples
loop.output: One candidate code or processing-model change in an isolated development branch
loop.check: Technician checks coordinate handling, geometry operations, attribute semantics and errors against the design, then independently tests representative and failing cases
loop.stop: One candidate; unknown interfaces, missing spatial assumptions or failed checks return to manual programming, with no merge or deployment
loop.why_not_simpler: Native GIS configuration is preferred; a model is used only for residual custom implementation where code structure must be drafted

steps.what: Test the implementation against independent GIS acceptance examples
Document the tested procedure and hand it to the application owner

tasks.design: Check native {OTHER} GIS configuration before writing custom code. For the remaining programming, use a bounded candidate draft against the technician's design and keep independent testing and handover with the technician; production release is separate.
tasks.previous_blocker: A clear design can still require substantial first-pass implementation writing.
tasks.enabler_now: Coding assistance can draft code for review without choosing the geographic model.
tasks.still_hard: Subtle spatial assumptions, edge cases and tests that merely repeat the implementation's mistake.
tasks.human_edge: The technician decides what geographic behaviour is correct.
tasks.altitude: Less initial code writing while design and acceptance remain accountable human work.

reach.learn: Explain geometry, identifiers and coordinate-system assumptions

evidence.claim: GitHub Copilot offers code completion, review and a background coding agent with expected oversight; this supports reviewed candidate implementation, not GIS correctness.
Model knowledge: spatial algorithms need independent geographic acceptance cases even when generated code runs successfully.

assumptions: Boundary is design, development, testing and internal handover; production deployment and ongoing application operation are excluded.

Technician captures user need, input and output schemas, coordinate systems, required operations and independent expected examples in s1's 25 hours, then records chosen interfaces and spatial rules in s2's 20 hours. Missing semantics stop drafting for manual clarification; no free model-produced acceptance flag is assumed.
Try native GIS configuration before custom code or a model; current software runtime earns no saving.
Draft stays in an isolated branch with no production credentials; source and test access must be approved locally.
unknowns: Residual custom-code volume after native configuration
research_questions: Does reviewed drafting reduce implementation effort after counting rejected code and spatial regression failures?

already_counted.description: Requirements, acceptance examples and design capture
Candidate code and spatial meaning checks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=89.5, gross=10.5 and net=6.5 after four upkeep hours. Range assumes useful first-pass custom code; design, tests and handover do not shrink.

role.altitude: Reduce repeated data conversion and initial code drafting while protecting geographic interpretation and validation.
reach: Explain spatial data constraints to analysts and database architects
role.ambitious_version: A GIS technician who can reproduce routine processing reliably and explain the limits of every resulting dataset.
